links.comparator_used: Rule-based baseline without Safety Agent gating
links.outcome: False inclusion rate in NSCLC trial pre-screening
links.effect: False inclusion fell from 11.63% to 1.16% in the combined 120-pair cohort (McNemar p = 0.002) and from 12.12% to 1.52% in the held-out set
links.tradeoff: Uncertain rate increased (more cases abstained or deferred)
links.quote: Safety Agent gating reduced the false inclusion rate from 11.63% to 1.16% in the combined 120-pair cohort (McNemar's test, p = 0.002) and from 12.12% to 1.52% in the held-out set, accompanied by an increase in uncertain rate.

links.outcome: False inclusion rate, accuracy and uncertain rate in trial pre-screening
links.effect: Multi-agent M1 and M2 had zero false inclusion on the structured cohort, with uncertain rates of 25.8% and 1.7%. The single-agent LLM also had zero false inclusion, the highest accuracy (0.74) and a 7.5% uncertain rate. In PMC real-text validation, M1 had 0/44 false inclusions and M2 had one.
links.tradeoff: M1 had a high uncertain rate (25.8%). M2 produced one false inclusion from an anomalous Safety Agent label upgrade on ambiguous unstructured text.
links.quote: Multi-agent M1 and M2 also achieved zero observed false inclusion on the structured cohort with distinct uncertainty profiles (25.8% and 1.7% uncertain, respectively); in the PMC real-text validation, M1 maintained zero false inclusion (0/44; 95% CI 0.0-8.0%) while M2 produced one false inclusion arising from an anomalous Safety Agent label upgrade on ambiguous unstructured text.

design_hint: safety agent gating and uncertainty-aware abstention
